title: Only A Fete
subtitle: The composition of all feasts is more or less the same.

items.text: Only A Fete
As night descends the following day, the once tranquil streets burst into life, abuzz with activity.
Bonfires crackled at the heart of the square, dispersing the chill and blending with the lively chatter, the scent of malt, and spices, to create a warmth that enveloped the whole crowd.

items.speaker: Resident
items.text: Could I have some bread? How much is it, today?

items.speaker: Vendor
items.text: All bread and meat are absolutely free today, courtesy of the City Council.

items.speaker: Resident
items.text: Free? But... what's going on here?
Before he could react, the vendor had already stuffed several loaves of bread into his hands.

items.speaker: Vendor
items.text: Here's your bread. And here, take a drink on the house.
The vendor bent down to pour an amber-colored ale from a nearby barrel.

items.speaker: Resident
items.text: A drink? This almost looks like elderberry malt to me...
As the resident took a sip from the cup. his face lit up.

items.speaker: Resident
items.text: This is elderberry malt!

items.speaker: Resident
items.text: But, what are you doing? All liquors are banned now, even arcane brews...

items.speaker: Resident
items.text: Wait... could it be, is this all to celebrate the festival?!

items.speaker: Vendor
items.text: Don't worry. It's only a "market fair" today, my friend.
The vendor gave a shrug that hid their smile.

items.speaker: Resident
items.text: A market fair? This looks more like a celebration to me!

items.speaker: Resident
items.text: I was wondering why they started lighting up the square. It seems to me you're celebrating Christmas again!

items.speaker: Resident
items.text: Have you lost your minds?! Did you forget about the Duke's ban on celebrations?

items.speaker: Vendor
items.text: Not at all, relax friend. There's no celebration here, only a "market fair."
The vendor slyly winked at the nervous citizen.

items.speaker: Vendor
items.text: And this? No alcohol here. Only "fermented elderberry syrup" freshly bought from an arcanist.

items.speaker: Resident
items.text: But it sure tastes like—

items.speaker: Vendor
items.text: Oy, drop the act, mate. Haven't you been waiting for a "market fair" like the rest of us?
The citizen gazed down at the cup in his hand.

items.speaker: Resident
items.text: Well, if it's just a "market fair"... Just a 'market fair,' that's all it is...
He muttered it low, as if convincing himself.
Raising the cup, he gulped the smooth malted drink down.
"Gulp, gulp, gulp..."

items.speaker: Resident
items.text: Ah! Haven't had elderberry malt in ages! Packs more punch than my old homemade beer!

items.speaker: Vendor
items.text: Remember that's "fermented elderberry syrup," mate. Drink your fill; we've got more than enough for today.

items.speaker: Resident
items.text: Oh, of course, only "syrup" how silly of me.

items.speaker: Resident
items.text: What a wonderful "market fair" this is—all the better with some lovely "fermented elderberry syrup"!

items.speaker: Charlie
items.text: S-So many people...

items.speaker: Charlie
items.text: I haven't seen a place feel so... alive in ages.

items.speaker: The Fool
items.text: Of course, everyone's flocking here! It's in our nature, something we can't resist! Like moths to bright flame!

items.speaker: Jeffrey
items.text: We invited a great many singers and actors... Though, for obvious reasons, only a few could make it as planned.

items.speaker: The Fool
items.text: It makes our planned performance all the more special, don't you think?

items.speaker: Jeffrey
items.text: You're right!

items.speaker: Jeffrey
items.text: I think the People's Troupe is what everyone's most looking forward to. That's why we've arranged your performance to be our grand finale.

items.speaker: Jeffrey
items.text: It should be a most spectacular show.
A wooden stage covered with tents stood at the square's center, poised to become the highlight of this unspoken festival.

items.speaker: Charlie
items.text: You mean we—we're, the last performance?

items.speaker: Charlie
items.text: If I'm not mistaken, our play would be...

items.speaker: The Fool
items.text: Yes—You'll play an important role in it.

items.speaker: Charlie
items.text: No, I absolutely can't do it!

items.speaker: Charlie
items.text: This... This is far too rash a decision! I'm sure I'll muck it up ...

items.speaker: The Fool
items.text: It was a collective decision, my dear Troupe Master.

items.speaker: The Fool
items.text: And we have full faith in your abilities.

items.speaker: Old Man
items.text: Huh?

items.speaker: Old Man
items.text: You...you're from the King's Troupe, aren't you? Here for the "market fair" too?

items.speaker: Charlie
items.text: Oh... Are you... talking to us?

items.speaker: Old Man
items.text: Of course, young lady. I've seen the King's Troupe perform, and I recognize a fair few of the faces among you.

items.speaker: Old Man
items.text: Well, whether you were for the "King" or the "Minister" once, those titles have long been lost.

items.speaker: Old Man
items.text: With all festivals and theater prohibited. Soon, your troupes may disappear altogether.

items.speaker: Old Man
items.text: Festivals and theater!

items.speaker: Old Man
items.text: I always thought they were an untouchable part of our lives, but now, they've become unspeakable sins.

items.speaker: Old Man
items.text: No matter how I try to reason with myself, I just can't understand why...

items.speaker: The Fool
items.text: A tyrant's sin is born of unearned glory. To keep his power and fame, he will abandon all conscience.

items.speaker: The Fool
items.text: Our existence is a mockery of the tyrant.

items.speaker: The Fool
items.text: And a tyrant cannot endure mockery.

items.speaker: Charlie
items.text: Mm... Mr. Fool! You can't speak like that here!

items.speaker: Old Man
items.text: I watched your performances back then when you were known as the King's Troupe.

items.speaker: Old Man
items.text: I saw actors dressed in splendid costumes lined up on either side. Then, the protagonist entered, greeted with thunderous applause.

items.speaker: Old Man
items.text: Goodness, that was an outstanding play... Something I'll never forget!

items.speaker: Old Man
items.text: The theater, props, costumes, scenery—everything was so magnificent!

items.speaker: Charlie
items.text: Th-thank you for your praise... I'm sorry to say, I wasn't part of the troupe at that time...

items.speaker: Old Man
items.text: What a pity! Those were beautiful times... So different from now.

items.speaker: Jeffrey
items.text: I understand how you must feel. The more darker the night, the more we yearn for the daylight long past.

items.speaker: Jeffrey
items.text: I fear we might never witness such a scene again.

items.speaker: Old Man
items.text: Oh... You're right. Bringing it up only adds to the regret.

items.speaker: Old Man
items.text: The king's troupe has disbanded, the old theaters will be demolished, and soon... all these splendid plays will be forgotten. With none left to remember their brilliant performances.

items.speaker: Charlie
items.text: T-that's not true.

items.speaker: Charlie
items.text: They will live on. Through generations, in writings and in memories.

items.speaker: Charlie
items.text: They won't vanish... Not as long as people have hope in their hearts. No, they won't disappear!

items.speaker: Charlie
items.text: Whether it's dazzling costumes or crude rags, whether in crowded theaters or in the dark of the woods

items.speaker: Charlie
items.text: As long as people have hope, they'll hold true to their hearts' desires.

items.speaker: Charlie
items.text: So, we'll deliver a performance just as outstanding as those of the past.

items.speaker: Charlie
items.text: No, more! I vow to you that we'll deliver a performance that surpasses all expectations.

items.speaker: The Fool
items.text: I vouch for this with all the skill and artistry I have left to give.

items.speaker: Old Man
items.text: I see now...

items.speaker: Old Man
items.text: The theater isn't about splendid costumes, but each actor's performance, the heart they bring to their role—A simple truth, long forgotten.

items.speaker: Old Man
items.text: I underestimated your determination... I will look forward to your performance tonight, young lady.
The old man's eyes sparkled as if a star was reborn in his eyes, and he smiled as he left the square.

items.speaker: The Fool
items.text: A splendid monologue, Troupe Master Charlie.

items.speaker: Charlie
items.text: I-I just... What was I even saying?!

items.speaker: Charlie
items.text: Bwaahhh... I'm so embarrassed...

items.speaker: Jeffrey
items.text: You shouldn't be. I'm sure of it now your troupe's performance will win over everyone.

items.speaker: Jeffrey
items.text: As the master of ceremonies, I should apologize, for putting you in the limelight but—

items.speaker: The Fool
items.text: It is plain to see everyone has high hopes for us, Troupe Master Charlie.

items.speaker: Charlie
items.text: Waaahhh... The pressure— it's too much! My stomach is turning...

items.speaker: The Fool
items.text: And yet the show must go on, my dear Troupe Master!

items.speaker: The Fool
items.text: As performers, it's our sacred mission to channel the audience's enthusiasm into our very best performance.

items.speaker: Charlie
items.text: Waaah! Make all the claims you like... But, if we mess up, we're done for!

items.speaker: The Fool
items.text: There's no need to panic. We will step on the stage and let our performance bring smiles or tears to the people.

items.speaker: The Fool
items.text: It's our calling, an unspoken bond between performers and audience.

items.speaker: Soldier
items.text: Mr. Jeffrey!
A breathless soldier, hurries to Jeffrey's side.

items.speaker: Soldier
items.text: Mr. Jeffrey, it's all gone wrong!

items.speaker: Jeffrey
items.text: What's wrong, soldier? Take heart, the festival is starting soon.

items.speaker: Soldier
items.text: It's the Duke's cavalry...

items.speaker: Soldier
items.text: The Duke's cavalry are approaching!

items.speaker: Jeffrey
items.text: What?!
TO BE CONTINUED ...
